edges.description: Null and heterozygous mice develop age-dependent lens light scattering after normal fetal lens development.
edges.limitations: Mice develop scattering postnatally and progressively, whereas some human families have congenital cataract; human missense and splice alleles are not modelled.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive juvenile onset cataract associated with mutation in BFSP1.
evidence.snippet: This is the first report of a mutation in the BFSP1 gene associated with human inherited cataracts.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mega-deletion in BFSP1 causing autosomal recessive juvenile cataract in a Pakistani consanguineous family.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) in an affected family member revealed a homozygous, intragenic 15.40 kb mega-deletion NG_012423.2; g.17485448_17500744del (chr20: 17,485,448-17,500,744-GRCh37/hg19) including three consecutive exons 3, 4, and 5, encompassing two domains of beaded filament structural protein 1 (BFSP1).

evidence.reference_title: Sporadic and Familial Congenital Cataracts: Mutational Spectrum and New Diagnoses Using Next-Generation Sequencing.
evidence.snippet: The proband was found to be compound heterozygous for mutations in BFSP1 (c.1492del p.(Ser498Leufs*24) and c.812T>C p.(Ile271Thr)).

evidence.reference_title: A novel beaded filament structural protein 1 (BFSP1) gene mutation associated with autosomal dominant congenital cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing revealed a heterozygous G>A transversion at c.1042 of the coding sequence in exon 7 of BFSP1 (c.1042G>A) in all affected members, which resulted in the substitution of a wild-type aspartate to an asparagine (D348N).

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations identified in Chinese families with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts by targeted next-generation sequencing.
evidence.snippet: Pedigree of Family 3, all patients carried the heterozygous mutation c.1804G > C in BFSP1.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted Exome Sequencing of Congenital Cataracts Related Genes: Broadening the Mutation Spectrum and Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in 27 Chinese Han Families.
evidence.snippet: (G) Reverse sequencing showed c.625 + 3A > G mutation of BFSP1gene in patients from family 19.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic genetic variants identified in Australian families with paediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: A novel BFSP1 c.1124delA p.(Glu375GlyfsTer2) frameshift variant segregated in an autosomal dominant manner in family CSA182 (figure 1G).

nodes.description: Recessive alleles are exon deletions predicted to shift the reading frame (exon 6; exons 3-5) or truncate the tail domain; dominant alleles include tail-domain missense (D348N, G602R), a splice-site variant and a tail-domain frameshift. In HEK293T cells the D348N mutant was expressed at lower levels than wild type. Whether dominant alleles act by haploinsufficiency or by interfering with filament co-assembly has not been resolved; mouse heterozygotes for a null allele do develop mild light scattering.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive juvenile onset cataract associated with mutation in BFSP1.
evidence.snippet: Direct sequencing revealed a 3343 bp deletion including exon 6 (c.736-1384_c.957-66 del) predicted to result in a shift of the open reading frame.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mega-deletion in BFSP1 causing autosomal recessive juvenile cataract in a Pakistani consanguineous family.
evidence.snippet: The large deletion potentially forced the junction of exon 2 with exon 6 at mRNA level and resulting in the shift of open reading frame.

evidence.reference_title: Sporadic and Familial Congenital Cataracts: Mutational Spectrum and New Diagnoses Using Next-Generation Sequencing.
evidence.snippet: In our patient (Family 46), the missense mutation affects the rod domain and the frameshift is predicted to lead to loss of part of the tail domain, highlighting the critical nature of these regions in the functions of BFSP1 required for lens clarity

evidence.reference_title: D348N Mutation of BFSP1 Gene in Congenital Cataract: it Does Matter.
evidence.snippet: BFSP1 mutation significantly decreases the expression of BFSP1 protein, weakened the ability of cell proliferation and increased apoptosis.

nodes.description: Filensin and CP49 do not form filaments alone; they co-assemble into the lens-specific beaded filament. Without filensin, CP49 levels fall and no beaded filaments form in fiber cells.

evidence.reference_title: Seeing is believing! The optical properties of the eye lens are dependent upon a functional intermediate filament cytoskeleton.
evidence.snippet: Whilst CP49 self-assembles into thick bundles of filaments, filensin only forms short fibrils, but when combined together they form filaments.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of the lens fiber cell-specific intermediate filament protein filensin.
evidence.snippet: The lens fiber cell-specific intermediate filament protein filensin is essential for beaded filament assembly.

nodes.description: Removal of the opacified lens with optical correction is the standard management of visually significant congenital and juvenile cataract; no BFSP1-specific therapy exists.
Cataract present at birth or in early childhood, reported in both recessive and dominant families; morphology ranges from nuclear to total opacity.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive juvenile onset cataract associated with mutation in BFSP1.
evidence.snippet: A genome wide scan in a consanguineous family of Indian origin with autosomal recessive developmental cataracts was performed by two-point linkage analysis with 382 microsatellite markers.

evidence.reference_title: A novel beaded filament structural protein 1 (BFSP1) gene mutation associated with autosomal dominant congenital cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: To identify the disease-causing mutation in a five-generation Chinese family affected with bilateral congenital nuclear cataract.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations identified in Chinese families with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts by targeted next-generation sequencing.
evidence.snippet: (c) The patient (III3) in Family 3 showed a total cataract.

nodes.description: Cataract developing in childhood or adolescence. The recessive Pakistani family was ascertained for juvenile cataract; the original Indian family's report is titled juvenile onset, but its abstract describes the cataract only as developmental.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mega-deletion in BFSP1 causing autosomal recessive juvenile cataract in a Pakistani consanguineous family.
evidence.snippet: Objective of the study was to delineate the underlying causative genetic defect for autosomal recessive juvenile cataract (ARJC) in an affected consanguineous multiplex, multigenerational Pakistani consanguineous family.

nodes.description: Progressive lamellar punctate cataract was reported in a proband with a heterozygous BFSP1 splice-site variant (c.625+3A>G).

evidence.reference_title: Targeted Exome Sequencing of Congenital Cataracts Related Genes: Broadening the Mutation Spectrum and Genotype-Phenotype Correlations in 27 Chinese Han Families.
evidence.snippet: (K) Photograph of proband in family 19 showed a lamellar punctate cataract.

evidence.reference_title: Pathogenic genetic variants identified in Australian families with paediatric cataract.
evidence.snippet: Sutural, often pulverulent-like, cataracts are the most frequently reported phenotype with BFSP2 variants while the range of phenotypes observed for BFSP1 variants is wider and includes nuclear, lamellar and cortical cataracts.

nodes.description: Light scattering begins after fetal development and worsens with age in filensin-null mice; heterozygous mice show a milder, later scattering. In patients this corresponds to congenital, infantile or juvenile lens opacity.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of the lens fiber cell-specific intermediate filament protein filensin.
evidence.snippet: Filensin knockouts began to show evidence of light-scattering by 2 months and worsened with age.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of the lens fiber cell-specific intermediate filament protein filensin.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous animals exhibited an intermediate phenotype, showing a reduction in filensin transcript and moderate light-scattering at 5 months.

evidence.reference_title: Functions of the intermediate filament cytoskeleton in the eye lens.
evidence.snippet: Evidence generated in studies in both mice and humans suggests a critical role for these proteins and their filamentous polymers in establishing the optical properties of the eye lens and in maintaining its transparency.

nodes.description: In filensin-null mouse lenses, fiber cells elongate and lose organelles normally but later lose their differentiated phenotype and the long-range stacking needed for clarity. Beaded filament loss also alters lens size, shape, stiffness and the refractive index gradient.
nodes.id: Loss of Fiber Cell Architecture and Long-Range Order

evidence.reference_title: Resisting the effects of aging: a function for the fiber cell beaded filament.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent to those stages, however, fiber cells undergo loss of the differentiated fiber cell phenotype and loss of the long-range stacking that characterizes fiber cells and that has been considered essential for clarity.

evidence.reference_title: Seeing is believing! The optical properties of the eye lens are dependent upon a functional intermediate filament cytoskeleton.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that the lens-specific beaded filaments are the key cytoskeletal element in organising and maintaining lens fibre cell architecture and are a key factor in determining the optical properties of the lens.
